summary: Phase 149O.19.5E.2 -- HMIC v1.1 Validator/Admin Implementation Identity Contract Independent Verification: INDEPENDENT-CONTRACT-VERIFICATION-ONLY phase re-deriving every claim of 149O.19.5E.1 from primary sources rather than trusting its phase summary or test constants. Confirmed baseline via direct inspection: repo clean at phase entry, origin/main..HEAD=0, 149O.19.5E.1 completed/complete, HMIC v1.1 frozen, production still 22-file, hardcoded False unchanged, no readiness integration, no real certification state, HATP production NOT READY, runtime Observed/observe/unavailable. Mechanically re-extracted 144 requirements (HMIC-REQ-001-144, gapless, unique), 12 CIVCs, and 34 attack rows directly from the live HMIC-001 contract text (not phase-summary prose, not copied test constants). Independently re-parsed HMIC-REQ-050's 24-file enumeration straight from the contract, confirming all 24 paths exist, are unique, regular, non-symlink, and repository-relative, and that all 22 original v1.0 paths are preserved byte-for-byte. Independently classified both new files (src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_certification.py, scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py) as authority-sensitive via a fresh AST/source dependency walk from each, finding zero additional unbound PCAE-owned authority-sensitive dependencies -- the 24-file transitive closure is sufficient. Independently re-derived the HMIC-REQ-054-058 implementation-identity digest algorithm from scratch (a fresh, from-scratch reimplementation, not by importing or trusting the production digest function) to confirm the self-reference argument is non-circular (mutating either the validator or admin script's modeled bytes changes the digest; no certification artifact, active-binding file, or revocation record is itself hashed) and to reproduce, digest-level, that a historical v1.0/22-file certification cannot satisfy v1.1 (rejected, no grandfathering) and that the stale 22-file production scope does not equal the 24-file v1.1 implementation identity. Verified HMIC-REQ-052's broadened closure rule explicitly covers HMIC's own validator/admin semantics; verified CIVC-4's strengthened text expresses self-binding/implementation-completeness; verified attack rows 11 (transitive implementation drift), 33 (validator self-modification/self-reference), and 34 (admin modification/old-scope replay) map to concrete normative clauses with deterministic outcomes. Confirmed production remains deliberately stale at 22 files (mechanically re-inspected, not trusted from any phase report), the hardcoded False readiness ceiling is unchanged, hatp_mandatory_cutover.py does not call the HMIC validator, zero readiness/cutover callers exist anywhere in src/pcae/**, and no real certification state exists on host (certifications.json / certification-bindings.json absent under HATPTrustStore.production().root) -- the fail-closed proof holds under direct inspection. Found and disclosed one new non-blocking finding: contract Sec42 (HMIC-REQ-139) and part of Sec46 still literally read 'HMIC-001 v1.0,' never synchronized when the header/Sec50 bumped to v1.1 -- a textual-consistency gap, not a semantic ambiguity (the header and Sec50 enumeration are unambiguous, and this finding is itself test-covered). Added tests/test_phase_149o_19_5e_2_hmic_v1_1_contract_independent_verification.py (26 tests, all independently derived -- none copied from 149O.19.5E.1's constants), covering the v1.0/v1.1 diff, independent 24-file extraction, transitive-closure verification, self-reference and admin-source digest-mutation tests, v1.0-replay and old-22-scope-under-v1.1 mismatch tests, production-staleness and fail-closed assertions, and the 144/12/34 counts. Reproduced historical HMIC suite and Fast Green results against the phase-entry commit (a8282578) via a temporary git worktree (removed after use) to confirm all observed failures are pre-existing, not introduced by this phase. Full '-k "hmic or hatp or 149o"' sweep and Fast Green raw counts match the pre-existing baseline exactly (38 pre-existing failures including the expected production-still-22 divergence, test_phase_149o_19_5b_hmic_identity_derivation.py::TestFrozenFileManifest::test_manifest_matches_contract_enumeration_exactly, unchanged by this phase) plus one additional xdist-only flake (tests/test_backend_cli.py::TestBackendReviewCreate::test_create_persists_to_latest -- fails only under -n auto parallel execution, passes deterministically in isolation, unrelated to HMIC/HATP). Clean deselected Fast Green run (all 39 named explicitly): 0 failed, 6051 passed, 2 skipped. Explicitly did NOT modify src/pcae/**, scripts/**, HMIC-001, or any of the other seven bound contracts; did not align production 22->24; did not integrate readiness; did not change the hardcoded False ceiling; did not create real certification state; did not activate HATP_MANDATORY; did not provision Class-B; did not modify Permission Broker or POL-005; did not implement COMP-002. Verdict: HMIC-001 v1.1 VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- VALIDATOR/ADMIN IMPLEMENTATION IDENTITY CONTRACT EVOLUTION CONFORMS. Transitive closure: sufficient (YES). Self-reference: CLOSED AT CONTRACT LEVEL. V1.0 replay: REJECTED. Production divergence: EXPECTED, FAIL-CLOSED, ALIGNMENT REQUIRED. W-1: CONTRACT EVOLUTION INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED -- PRODUCTION 24-FILE ALIGNMENT PENDING -- NOT CLOSED (not CLOSED; not READY FOR WAVE F). B-149O.19.3-1 remains independently closed. B-149O-1..4 verdict unchanged, carried forward: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED AT SYSTEM IMPLEMENTATION/ENFORCEMENT BOUNDARY -- DEPLOYMENT/OPERATIONAL ACTIVATION DEFERRED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable.
